question: Why is the magnetic polaron formation time shorter than the circular polarization evolution time scale in type-II Zn,MnTe/ZnSe quantum dots under a magnetic field?
answer: The magnetic polaron formation time is shorter than the circular polarization evolution time scale in type-II Zn,MnTe/ZnSe quantum dots due to the distinct mechanisms governing each process. Magnetic polaron formation arises from the rapid alignment of Mn spins around the hole, driven by strong exchange interactions, while the slower circular polarization evolution reflects the gradual spin relaxation of the hole itself under the magnetic field. Time-resolved photoluminescence measurements reveal a red-shift in transition energies and a small splitting of circularly polarized components, confirming that polaron formation precedes full polarization development. This difference in timescales is attributed to the faster spin ordering of localized Mn moments compared to the hole spin dynamics.
